1. # **Introduction**

   1. ## **Project Purpose, Objectives, and Success Criteria**

*Our UNO Project is a Java-based game that intends to recreate the original UNO card game in a new style. The game takes the common UNO mechanics and adds custom cards, powers, progression, and difficulty across multiple levels. The purpose of the project is to create a playable, unique concept of a familiar game, with changes that are more engaging and interesting.*

*Primary objectives and needs to be satisfied are as follows:*

* *A unique, UNO-style game built in Java*  
* *Add custom cards and effects that enhance gameplay*  
* *Implement level-based progression with increasingly difficult AI opponents*  
* *Provide a development environment and product similar to those in the industry*

*Success criteria for the project are as follows:*

* *The game has a complete, playable gameplay loop*  
* *Players can progress through multiple, increasingly difficult levels*  
* *Players can play locally with friends*  
* *AI opponents function reliably and engagingly*  
* *Custom cards and effects are integrated seamlessly with the core gameplay*  
* *The project sufficiently shows the intended game concept*

*This project team consists of a small team of just two, and is intended as a small prototype as opposed to a fully fledged game release.*

2. ## **Document Conventions**

* *Requirements will be labeled: REQ-\#:*  
* *Assumptions will be labeled: AS-\#:*  
* *Dependencies will be labeled: DE-\#:*  
* *Constraints will be labeled: CO-\#:*  
* *“Shall” refers to a mandatory requirement*  
* *Section headings are labeled and are in bold for easy identification.*  
* *Requirements may be assigned priority levels: High, Medium, and Low.*

  3. ## **Intended Audience and Reading Suggestions**

*This document is intended for developers, project managers, marketing staff, users, testers, and document writers. This document contains all necessary information regarding the development and work process of the UNO project. It is organized with the description of the project being first, followed by features, and finally ending with requirements. Referring to the glossary is highly recommended regardless of one’s purpose in reading this document. People who only need more surface level information may refer to section 1.4, 2.1, and 2.2. For people who are more interested in the code, section 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.7, 3, and 4 are all important.*

4. ## **Project Scope**

*The UNO game project is a digital implementation of the card game UNO. The goal of the software is to recreate the game in a digital setting. This recreation includes the rules, the cards, valid moves, and progression of the game.*   
*The objective of this project is to ensure that proper procedures are followed. Turn order, game state, and automation of rules are all procedures that should be covered. The application will be playable in a single player environment against AI opponents that can have different difficulty. Same screen multiplayer will also be available, being playable via passing the used device.* 

5. ## **Project Deliverables**

The project deliverables are as follows:

* A playable, Java–based UNO game

* Core UNO rules implemented

* Custom card and effect system

* Enemy AI and difficulty

* Game progression through multiple levels

* User interface for display and game interaction

* Documentation with project installation, gameplay, and technical information

* Source code repository with version control and a maintainable structure

  6. ## **References**

*The following materials were used as references for this Project Management Plan:*

* [*UNO Rules*](https://www.unorules.com/) *and reference materials used by the project team.*

2. # **Overall Description**

   1. ## **Product Perspective**

*This project is a digital recreation of the card game UNO. It will follow the basic principles of UNO in the sense that the cards will be from the UNO card game and the main goal of the game will be the same as the original game.*

2. ## **Product Features**

*The major features of this UNO project are:*

* *Game Setup: The system will allow the player to customize rules and initialize the game to be based around these rules. This can be the number of opponents, difficulty of opponents, and customizable number of cards in the deck that will all follow either standard UNO rules or customized rules.*  
* *Card Mechanics: Players will be able to view their cards, the last card that has been played, and any valid cards that can be played. The system will manage any special cards such as Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Draw Four Wild, Wild. Along with any card stacking mechanics.*  
* *Turn Management: The system will be able to keep track of whose turn it is, along with any special cards that might change the order of turns.*  
* *Computer-Controlled Opponents: The system will allow the player to select AI, along with their difficulties, to play with.*   
* *Game Completion: The system will detect when a player has no cards left and declare that player the winner.*

  3. ## **Evolution of the Plan**

*This Project Management plan will be updated and maintained as needed throughout the three planned project phases:*

*Phase 1: Project Management Plan, Due on Sep 27, 2026*   
*Phase 2: Project Implementation \- Iterative 1, Due on Oct 24, 2026*   
*Phase 2: Project Implementation \- Iterative 2, Due on Nov 14, 2026*   
*Phase 3: Project Implementation and Testing, Due on Dec 6, 2026* 

*In addition to the three scheduled phase-completion updates, the plan may be updated as needed when:*

* *A significant risk materializes or a new risk is identified*  
* *Scope changes are made (e.g., new cards, powers, gameplay modes, or progression features)*  
* *AI difficulty levels or opponent behavior are substantially modified*  
* *Testing identifies a critical technical, usability, or performance issue*  
* *Schedule or resource constraints change unexpectedly*  
* *Accessibility requirements are added, removed, or reprioritized*  
* *A project decision requires formal documentation*

4. ## **User Classes and Characteristics**

*Player (Primary Users): They will interact with the system by clicking on menu options, viewing their cards, playing cards, and any other gameplay elements. They are expected to know the basics of keyboard and mouse interaction. Players will rely on the system and interface in order to know what is happening and what they are doing when they click.*  
*AI Opponents: These are AI that will simulate human opponents. They follow much of the same system as the players, but their decision making will be different depending on the difficulty they are set to.* 

5. ## **Operating Environment**

*This UNO project will operate on a standard computer system.*   
*The environment is defined as the following:*

* *Platform: A computer with a keyboard, mouse, and display.*  
* *Operating System: Windows 10 or later, macOS, or Linux operating system that have Java Runtime Environment.*  
* *Programming Environment: Java programming language*  
* *Runtime Requirement: Java Runtime Environment version 8 or higher*  
* *Graphics: Standard graphical libraries provided by Java*

  6. ## **Design and Implementation Constraints**

  *CO-1: The project must be implemented in Java or remain compatible with the Java-based development requirements established for the project.*

  *CO-2: The application must run on a standard personal computer with a supported Java Runtime Environment.*

  *CO-3: Development is constrained by the available time, experience, and effort of the two-person project team.*

  *CO-4: The initial release is constrained to local, single-device gameplay. Online multiplayer is outside the current project scope.*

  *CO-5: The gameplay rules and logic remain consistent with base UNO rules.*

  *CO-6: The system must support computer-controlled opponents, including selectable difficulty levels, if those features remain part of the initial release.*

  *CO-7: The application must be designed to run acceptably on lower-end systems, particularly during menus and normal gameplay.*

  7. ## **User Documentation**

*In-game instructions will be provided to the player. It will show what each button does when pressed. There will also be a README file included with the game for basic controls.* 

8. ## **Assumptions and Dependencies**

   1. Assumptions

   *AS-1: The project will be developed primarily as a Java application*

   *AS-2: The game concept will remain focused on a rogue-like interpretation of UNO*

   *AS-3: The project will target personal computers running Windows 10 or later, with access to a keyboard, mouse, and display, as well as Java Runtime Environment version 8 or higher.*

   *AS-4: Players have a basic understanding of the game UNO*

   *AS-5: User progress, settings, textures, sounds, and other required data will be stored locally when those features are implemented.*

   *AS-6: The game engine and final visual style remain subject to project decisions and may change as development continues.*

   *AS-7: The initial release will support single-player gameplay against computer-controlled opponents, as well as local play.*

      2. Dependencies

   *DE-1: The project depends on the Java programming language and Java Runtime Environment version 8 or higher.*

   *DE-2: The project depends on standard Java libraries and graphical libraries.*

   *DE-3: Development depends on an integrated development environment or code editor, currently identified as Visual Studio Code.*

   *DE-4: The project depends on the GitHub repository coelacanth-64/Roguelike-UNO for source-code storage, version control, and collaboration.*

   *DE-5: The game depends on local access to any required texture, audio, save-data, and configuration files.*

   *DE-6: AI gameplay depends on the implementation of opponent decision-making logic and difficulty levels.*

   *DE-7: Level progression, custom cards, powers, and additional gameplay modes depend on the completion of the core card, turn, and game-state systems.*

   *DE-8: Save and resume functionality depends on the design and implementation of a reliable local file-storage mechanism.*

   *DE-9: Accessibility features depend on the selected user-interface technology and the time available for implementation and testing.*

   *DE-10: Requirements and scope depend on decisions regarding the game’s visual style, setting, custom cards, powers, and gameplay modes.*

3. # **System Features**

   1. ## **Game Initialization**

*4.1.1	Description and Priority*

*Game Initialization will allow a user to start a new game of UNO and prepare the system for gameplay. During this process the system will create a deck, shuffle the cards, distribute  play hands, and set up the initial card in the discard pile.*  
*Priority: High*

*4.1.2	Stimulus/Response Sequences*

1. *User selects start new game option*  
2. *The system prompts the user to select the number of players and AI*  
3. *The user selects and confirms their choice*  
4. *The system shuffles the deck and distributes the starting cards to each player*  
5. *The system places the first card on the discard pile*  
6. *The system determines the first players’ turn and begins gameplay*

*4.1.3	Functional Requirements*

*REQ-1: The system shall allow a user to start a new UNO game*  
*REQ-2: The system shall create a UNO deck based on the settings set by the user*  
*REQ-3: The system shall shuffle the cards before distributing them*  
*REQ-4: The system shall deal seven cards to each player at the start of the game*  
*REQ-5: The system shall place one card face up in the discard pile to begin game*  
*REQ-6: The system shall determine which player goes first*

2. ## **Player Turn Management**

*4.2.1	Description and Priority*

*Player turn management controls the order the game is played in. It tracks the current player and the player that will play next. It will also handle any card that changes the turn order, such as skip or reverse.*

*Priority: High*

*4.2.2	Stimulus/Response Sequences*

1. *The system identifies the first player to start the game*  
2. *The current player is prompted to make a move*   
3. *The player selects a valid card or chooses to draw cards*  
4. *The system tests the card chosen against the one at the top of the discard pile*  
5. *The system applies the affect, if any, of the card played*  
6. *The system updates the current player to the next player in the turn order*  
7. *Steps 2-6 repeat until one card is left*  
8. *If a player has one card left, they must press the UNO button before the opponent does*  
9. *If a player plays their last card, they win*

*4.2.3	Functional Requirements*

		*REQ-1: The system shall maintain the current player’s identity throughout the game*

		*REQ-2: The system shall prompt the current player to take a turn when it is their turn*

		*REQ-3: The system shall validate the player’s move according to the current top card on the discard pile and the game rules* 

		*REQ-4: The system shall enforce special card effects that alter turn order, such as Skip or Reverse cards*

		*REQ-5: The system shall automatically update to the next player’s turn after the current player has completed a valid move*

		*REQ-6: The system shall prevent players from taking a turn out of order*

		*REQ-7: The system shall notify all players of the current players’ move and any changes in turn order*

3. ## **Card Play Test**

*4.3.1	Description and Priority*

*The Card Play Test feature ensures that every card played by a player follows the rules in the settings. The system checks that the card matches the top card on the discard pile by color, number, or symbol, and prevents illegal moves. This feature also handles when a player has to draw a card due to having no valid moves.*

*Priority: High*

*4.3.2	Stimulus/Response Sequences*

1. *The current player selects a card*  
2. *The system compares the selected card with the top card in the discard pile*  
3. *If the card matches the color, number, or symbol, the system accepts the play*  
4. *If the card is invalid, the system rejects the play and prompts the player to choose another card or draw from the deck*  
5. *If no valid moves are available, the system automatically forces the player to draw a card*  
6. *The system updates the discard pile if the play is valid and applied any associated card effects*  
7. *If the player has only one card left, it will prompt the current player and all other players with an “UNO” button*  
8. *If the player presses it before anybody else, they are safe, otherwise they draw a card*

*4.3.3	Functional Requirements*

	*REQ-1: The system shall verify that a played card matches the top card on the discard pile by color, number, or symbol*

	*REQ-2: The system shall reject any card that does not meet the matching criteria*

	*REQ-3: The system shall notify the player when an invalid card is played and prompt them to select another card or draw from the deck*

	*REQ-4: The system shall automatically force the player to draw a card if no valid moves are available*

	*REQ-5: The system shall update the discard pile when a valid card is played*

	*REQ-6: The system shall apply any associated effects from the played card*

	*REQ-7: The system shall prompt all players when one player has a single card left*

	*REQ-8: The system shall force the player who has one card left to draw two if the player did not hit the “UNO” button first*

	*REQ-9: The system shall log all cards plays to maintain accurate game state*

4. ## **Special Card Effects**

*4.4.1	Description and Priority*

*The Special Card Effects feature will handle the unique interactions triggered by special UNO cards such as Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Draw Four Wild, and Wild. The system enforces the rules associated with these special cards and updates the game state accordingly.*

*Priority: High*

*4.4.2	Stimulus/Response Sequences*

1. *A player plays a special card*  
2. *The system identifies the type of special card played*  
3. *The system applies the effect according to the UNO rules:*  
- *Skip: Skip the next players turn*  
- *Reverse: Order of play is reversed*  
- *Draw Two: Next player draws two cards and loses their turn*  
- *Draw Four Wild: Next player draws four cards, loses their turn, and current player selects a color to play*  
- *Wild: Current player selects a color to play*  
4. *The system updates the current player and turn order accordingly*  
5. *The system notifies all players of the card effect and changes the current game state.*

*3.4.3	Functional Requirements*

	*REQ-1: The system shall detect when a special card is played and identify its type*

	*REQ-2: The system shall skip the next players’ turn if the Skip card is played*

	*REQ-3: The system shall reverse the turn order if the Reverse card is played*

	*REQ-4: The system shall make the next player draw two and skip their turn if a Draw Two card is played*

	*REQ-5: The system shall make the next player draw four, skip their turn, and let the current player pick a color to play if a Draw Four Wild card is played*

	*REQ-6: The system shall let the current player choose a color to play if a Wild card is played*

	*REQ-7: The system shall notify all players of the card played and the resulting game state change*

	*REQ-8: The system shall update the discard pile and maintain an accurate game state after a special card is played*

5. ## **Game End Detection**

*4.5.1	Description and Priority*

*The Game End Detection feature monitors the game state to determine when a player has met the winning conditions of having no cards left. It will then conclude the game. The system will then announce the winner and prevent further gameplay, until a new game is started.*

*Priority: High*

*4.5.2	Stimulus/Response Sequences*

1. *A player plays their last card*   
2. *The system detects that the player has no cards left*   
3. *The system checks if the player has fulfilled the winning conditions according to the rules*  
4. *The system announces the winner of the game*  
5. *The system ends the current game and prevents further moves*  
6. *The system prompts players to start a new game*

*4.5.3	Functional Requirements*

	*REQ-1: The system shall monitor the number of cards held by each player after every turn*

	*REQ-2: The system shall detect when a player has no cards remaining*

	*REQ-3: The system shall verify that the winning player has fulfilled the winning conditions according to the rules*

	*REQ-4: The system shall announce the winner to all players*

	*REQ-5: The system shall end the current game and prevent any further moves from other players*

	*REQ-6: The system shall provide the option to start a new game to the players*

	*REQ-7: The system shall restart all game state variables when a new game is started*

4. # **External Interface Requirements**

   1. ## **User Interfaces**

*The user interface is intended to be simple for the user to understand and navigate, while still being visually appealing. While customizability is a priority, that should not be at the expense of the users ability to understand menus, or at the cost of the speed of navigation.*

*While navigation is primarily intended to be done through a connected mouse, keyboard selection will also be included for ease of use, as well as keyboard shortcuts to certain menus, as needed. Examples of keyboard shortcuts may include, but are not limited to: ESC being used to pause the game, or enter a “pause menu”. Arrow Keys being used to navigate the menu and card hand, as well as Space or Enter being used to select an option or play a card. Other shortcuts could include buttons pressed to select a certain ability be used, or call out “Uno\!” when the second-to-last card is played.*

2. ## **Hardware Interfaces**

*The primary device used to interact with the game will be a personal computer. Given time, there may be support for mobile devices as well. The game will, nearly exclusively, use mouse controls to select cards, powers, and GUI choices. However, keyboard support may be used to navigate the menus and card selection screens, in order to make a more accessible experience. There will also be sound effects that will be audible through device speakers or headphones. These will be done simply through these devices connected through USB to the computer. If the game were to be playable on mobile devices, the touchscreen would be the only way to interface with the game.*

3. ## **Software Interfaces**

*The primary software interface that will be used are the files that contain the user save data, textures, and sounds. A file will be written to and read from that contains specific information that the program will take in order to store the user’s progress between different periods of playtime. There will also be texture and audio files that will be used.*

*Further software interfaces that are undecided as of writing include a game engine to help with development. These will be used for more extensive libraries and other game development related assets.*

4. ## **Communications Interfaces**

*There will be minimal use of communications interfaces. All interactions in the game are intended to be on one device, so there will be no need to make use of any form of external communication.*

5. # **Other Nonfunctional Requirements**

   1. ## **Performance Requirements**

*The product should perform well even on lower-end systems, especially in user interfaces and other menus, to ensure a smooth experience. While gameplay is intended to have minimal performance issues, some performance issues are expected, given the vast amount of options the user may have to change how the game may work. Some “runs” of then game may include combinations of cards, powers, or other features that could slow performance, which is expected.*

2. ## **Safety Requirements**

*A ‘saving’ feature will be included that will be used to allow the user to keep game progress as they revisit the game. This will be implemented by writing to a file on the user’s computer. The software will need to ensure that the file is written to a safe location on the user’s computer that will not lead to any kind of data loss for the user. Additionally, the program must be thoroughly tested and optimized to prevent performance issues for the user. This must be done to ensure that the personal devices of the user will not be harmed or damaged in any way that could introduce problems with other tasks the user may be doing.*

*Additionally, accessibility features should be included for users who need them, including features that could influence a user’s personal health.*  
*Examples include:* 

* *Features such as flashing lights, and screen shaking should have settings to lessen their effects.*  
* *Rebindable controls should be included for users with difficulty using default mouse or keyboard inputs.*  
* *Colorblind modes could be included to help users with difficulty telling card colors apart.*  
* *Graphics settings should be included to help users adjust other visual settings to a style that suits the individual.*  
* *Audio settings should be included for users who are hard of hearing, or may need audio to be lower.*

*The European Accessibility Act (EAA) is an example of an external policy that intends to improve software for those with accessibility needs.*

3. ## **Security Requirements**

*A ‘saving’ feature will be included that will be used to allow the user to keep game progress as they revisit the game. This will be implemented by writing to a file on the user’s computer, which will be designed to make sure that user data is not altered or viewed by the program, to ensure all user data is protected.*

4. ## **Software Quality Attributes**

*The product is intended to be very customizable, replayable, and portable, while still keeping high maintainability in order to continue adding and changing features as needed, in order for the gameplay to have a lot of depth in how the user plays each round. Despite this, the product is still intended to be simple for the user to understand, prioritizing the user’s experience and ease of use.*

* *Review of unresolved design issues, including engine selection, visual style, setting, cards, powers, and gameplay modes*

7. # **Managerial and Technical Process Plans**

   1. ## **Start-Up Plans**

Start-Up Plans will be prepared using the requirements, planned features, previous development experience, and the amount of time available for the project. Since this project is being developed by a two-person student team, estimates will focus primarily on development effort, schedule, and required resources rather than monetary cost. For that same reason we won’t really have any staff training plan.

1. Estimation Plans

*The team will use task decomposition and our own judgment to estimate the size and effort required for each feature.*   
*Large features will be divided into smaller tasks:* 

- *Designing the game system*   
- *Implementing cards*  
- *Creating the player system*   
- *Implementing encounters*  
- *Developing the user interface.* 

*Estimated effort will be recorded in hours and compared with the team's available development time.*  
*A Gantt chart will be used to estimate and track the project schedule. Git and GitHub will be used to track development progress and provide information about how long individual tasks take. NetBeans and Java will be used as the primary development environment and programming language.*  
*Both members of the development team will participate in creating and reviewing estimates. Each member will provide input based on their understanding of the requirements and the difficulty of the tasks. Re-estimations will be up to our discretion, but we did schedule for extra time in case any issues come up.*  
*![][image5]![][image6]*

2. Risk Management

*Risks will be prioritized based on their likelihood of occurring and their potential impact on the project's schedule, functionality, and quality. High-priority risks will be addressed first, with contingency plans created when appropriate. Risks will be addressed as they come up.*

3. Project Close-Out Plan

*At the end of the project, the team will verify that the completed game meets the required functionality and that all necessary testing and documentation have been completed. Any remaining critical bugs will be addressed before the final release. No additional staffing or maintenance is planned after the project is completed unless required by the course.*

**Appendix A: Glossary**

* *USB \- Universal Serial Bus (USB) specifies the communication protocols to and from a host device and an external peripheral device, such as mice, keyboards, and headphones.*  
* *AI: Artificial Intelligence. In this project, AI refers to computer-controlled opponents that make gameplay decisions based on their assigned difficulty level.*  
* *Rogue-like: A game style characterized by progression, difficulty scaling, and replayability.*  
* *UNO: The card game on which the project is based.*  
* *UI: User Interface; the visual and interactive layer of the game.*  
* *Run: A period of gameplay or progression through a particular sequence of levels, encounters, cards, or powers.*

**Appendix B: Issues List**

1. *The usage of a game development engine for the project is being decided, the primary candidates being LibGDX and Godot, to help speed up development and make graphics easier to implement.*  
2. *Another issue being discussed is the visual style of the game. The discussed styles include either pixel art, or low-poly graphics. Further, the setting is another issue being discussed, with the current concepts having a dungeon setting.*  
3. *Specific powers, cards, and gameplay modes are all issues being discussed, and will need further testing when the game is more developed to determine what features will be included in the final product.*
